title: Lensed page

source.author: siddharth (@buildwithsid)
source.how_it_was_built: unknown. The post gives no method and no code. The first two dozen replies were read on 2026-11-05; one asks how it was made and none answers.

reads_as: A page of typed notes with a black hole resting on it. The type bends around the hole, and the hole itself is set in type.

plate.texture: none. This is a screen piece.

page_text.status: draft, original. Replace freely. Never reuse the reference's copy.
page_text.rule: The text describes what the hole is doing to it. Short paragraphs, 4-space first-line indent, set solid from the origin to the right edge, repeated top to bottom until the page is full.
page_text.title_line: FIELD NOTES ON A HEAVY THING
paragraphs: This page is flat until something heavy is set down on it. After that, every line has to go around.
Light keeps a straight course. The space it crosses is what bends, and the heavy thing is what bent it.
So a letter behind the weight can reach you by two roads. You may see it twice. You may see it pulled into an arc. Line it up exactly and it becomes a ring.
Closer in, light can be caught in a circle around the weight. Light aimed any nearer than that does not come back, and that part of the page shows nothing.
The bright band is matter on its way in, hot enough to read by. The side turning toward you is the brighter side. The far side shows over the top, because its light went the long way round.
A letter that falls in does not vanish while you watch. It slows. It reddens. It dims. You lose the ability to read it long before it is gone.
Read this while it is still here.

hole.units: r_s, the Schwarzschild radius. Everything below scales from this one number.

regions.name: far field
regions.where: more than 13 r_s from the hole
regions.shows: the page character of that cell, untouched

regions.name: halo
regions.where: outside the disk image, inside 13 r_s
regions.shows: a page character taken from where the lens says the light came from, or nothing

regions.name: disk
regions.where: cells whose ray lands on the disk, r 3.0 to 9.5 r_s in the disk plane
regions.shows: a ramp glyph for the luminance of that spot on the disk

regions.name: shadow
regions.where: cells whose ray is captured (impact parameter under 2.598 r_s)

halo.lens_map: beta = theta * (1 - w(rho) * (theta_E / rho)^2); theta is the cell's offset from the hole in px, rho = |theta|; the cell shows page[round((hole + beta) / cell)]
halo.taper: w(rho) = 1 - smoothstep(8 r_s, 13 r_s, rho), so the map is the identity at the halo edge and the far field needs no special case

dropout.decision: hash(col, row, floor(t / 0.12 s)) < keep. A cell prints fully or not at all.

halo.hot_cells: a printed halo cell uses hot_ink with probability 0.004 per decision
halo.glyph_drawing: upright, unscaled, unrotated, full opacity, on the grid

geometry.orbit: clockwise seen from above, so the right side of the image approaches the viewer

ray.equation: x'' = -1.5 * h^2 * x / |x|^5, with h^2 = |x cross v|^2 fixed at launch and |v| = 1 (r_s = 1)
stop: |x| > 65 and moving outward: escaped, the cell is halo
first crossing of z = 0 with r_in <= r <= r_out: disk hit, record r, phi and the ray direction

luminance.doppler: 1 / (gamma * (1 - beta * dot(orbit_dir, photon_dir))), beta = sqrt(0.5 / (r - 1)), gamma = 1 / sqrt(1 - beta^2)
luminance.tex: 0.75 + 0.25 * noise(r, phi - omega(r) * t), omega(r) = 0.9 * (r_in / r)^1.5 rad/s
luminance.to_glyph: index = 1 + floor((L / L_max)^0.45 * (n - 1)), n = ramp length

ramp.rule: Re-sort this ramp by measured ink coverage in the glyph atlas for the face in use. The order above is by eye.

disk.hot_cells: a disk cell with L / L_max above 0.82 uses hot_ink with probability 0.35 per decision

bake.what: Trace once, in the hole's own frame, on a table of screen offsets. Per frame, each cell reads the table at (cell center - hole center). Only tex and the dropout change over time.
bake.cost: about 17,000 rays. Run it in idle chunks so first paint is not blocked.

verified.by: bake-prototype.js in this folder, run 2026-11-05 with Node
verified.bright_to_dim_side: 2.81 to 0.28, about 10 to 1, bright side on the right

motion.position: follows the pointer through a critically damped spring, time constant 0.9 s
motion.idle: after 2 s without pointer input, and in thumbnails, the hole wanders: hole = center + (0.22 * W * n1(0.035 t), 0.16 * H * n2(0.03 t)), n1 and n2 smooth noise in -1..1
motion.reduced_motion: hole fixed at (0.62 W, 0.45 H); no shimmer, no disk rotation; one static frame
motion.pause: stop all work on lens:pause. fragment-boot.js already holds requestAnimationFrame.

pass_order: page grid: every cell gets its page character
lens map: halo cells swap in the character from their source cell
dropout: halo cells print or go blank
disk: cells that hit the disk are overwritten with a ramp glyph
hot ink: a few printed cells change ink
draw: one glyph per printed cell from the atlas
pass_order_why: Dropout runs before the disk so it cannot punch holes in the disk. The shadow clears last so nothing prints inside it.
coupling: One mass at one position. r_s sets the shadow (2.598 r_s), the disk (3 to 9.5 r_s), the Einstein radius (5 r_s) and the halo edge (13 r_s), and the hole position moves all four together. The halo, the disk and the shadow cannot disagree about where the hole is or how heavy it is.
why_it_survives: Remove the remap and the halo is noise around a picture. Remove the disk and the bend has no cause. Remove the grid and it is an image filter over text.

measured_from_reference.grid: about 214 columns by 65 rows; cell about 5.6 by 11.0 px
measured_from_reference.pink: #d17691 averaged over antialiased, compressed pixels; the solid ink is more saturated
measured_from_reference.disk_px: bright ring to about 184 from center, faint glyphs to about 250
measured_from_reference.halo_px: text is untouched beyond about 340 from center; the boundary is close to a circle
measured_from_reference.hole_speed: 0.02 to 0.05 frame widths per second, direction changing every 8 to 12 s
measured_from_reference.page_copy: a self-describing essay under an all-caps title, repeated down the page

inferred: the lens formula, theta_E and the taper
dropout curve and shimmer rate (set by eye from frames 0.15 s apart)
that the hole follows a pointer; the video shows a slow wander and no cursor
disk radii, camera elevation and the luminance exponents (chosen so the bake matches the reference silhouette)

frame rate on a low-power laptop
